definition_zh: 噩梦；梦魇；可怕的处境；令人恐惧的经历
definition_en: a frightening dream, especially one that wakes the sleeper; a very unpleasant or frightening situation or experience

senses.title: A frightening dream that wakes the sleeper
senses.titleCN: 噩梦；惊醒人的可怕梦境
senses.definition: a frightening dream, usually so vivid that the sleeper wakes in fear
senses.definitionCN: 令人恐惧的梦，通常逼真到使睡着的人惊醒
senses.example: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。
senses.why: Old English niht meant night and mare named the demon believed to sit on a sleeper's chest, so the word began as a name for the pressure felt in the dark rather than for the story told afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 niht 是「夜」，mare 指传说中压在睡者胸口的恶魔，所以这个词最初命名的是黑暗中感到的那股压迫，而不是醒来后讲述的情节。

senses.title: The old demon held to sit on a sleeper's chest
senses.titleCN: 梦魇；旧指夜中压身的恶魔
senses.definition: in older use, an evil spirit believed to suffocate people in their sleep, together with the choking sensation it caused
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指被认为在睡眠中使人窒息的恶灵，以及它带来的压迫窒息感
senses.example: In the old tale, a nightmare crouched on the traveller's chest until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，一只梦魇蹲在旅人胸口直到天亮。
senses.why: Mare was a demon, not a horse, and the choking weight of sleep paralysis was explained as its body; the modern bad-dream sense grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: mare 是恶魔而不是母马，睡眠瘫痪时那种被压住的窒息感被解释成它的身体；现代「噩梦」的意思正是从这幅画面长出来的。

senses.title: A situation that feels like a bad dream
senses.titleCN: 可怕的处境；噩梦般的经历
senses.definition: a very unpleasant, difficult or frightening situation or experience
senses.definitionCN: 非常不愉快、艰难或令人恐惧的局面或经历
senses.example: The airport closure turned our trip into a nightmare.
senses.exampleCN: 机场关闭让我们的行程变成了一场噩梦。
senses.why: Once the word names a night terror, calling a day or a journey a nightmare borrows the same helpless fear into waking life, which is why the figurative use needs no new word.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词先命名夜里的恐惧，说某个白天或某趟行程是 nightmare，就是把这股无能为力的恐惧借到清醒生活里，所以比喻义不需要另造新词。

intro.en: Nightmare is a native English compound of night and a word for a demon, and its bad-dream sense is later than the demon it once named.
intro.cn: nightmare 是英语本土的复合词，由「夜」和一个指恶魔的词合成；「噩梦」义比它最初命名的恶魔出现得更晚。

items.en: Niht was the ordinary word for night and supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: niht 是古英语里表示「夜」的常用词，构成这个词的前半。

items.en: Mare named an evil spirit or incubus believed to press on sleepers, and it is a different word from mare meaning a female horse.
items.cn: mare 指被认为压住睡者的恶灵或梦淫妖，它与表示母马的 mare 是两个不同的词。

items.en: The compound first named the choking visitation and the terror that came with it, still close to the demon rather than to the dream.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初指夜间压身的侵扰和随之而来的恐惧，仍贴近恶魔本身而不是梦。

items.en: Writers began using nightmare for any frightening dream, and the demon faded into the background of the word; the exact date of this shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，十六至十七世纪的作者开始用 nightmare 指任何可怕的梦，恶魔渐渐退到这个词的背景里；这一转变的确切年代存疑。

items.en: Modern English keeps the dream sense and extends it to any miserable or frightening situation, as in a nightmare journey.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「噩梦」义，并把它扩展到任何糟糕或可怕的情形，如 a nightmare journey。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same night element or sharing the spelling mare; the near-meaning group collects words for bad dreams and the fear they leave behind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 night 成分构成的词，以及与 mare 拼写相同的词；近义组收表示噩梦和它留下的恐惧的词。

entries.definition: Built from nightmare with -ish, meaning like a nightmare.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nightmare 加 -ish 构成，义为「噩梦般的」。

entries.definition: A female horse, a separate word that merely shares the spelling of the demon in nightmare; the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 母马，只是与 nightmare 里的恶魔同形，两者来源无关。

entries.definition: The time when night begins, built with the same night element.
entries.definitionCN: 夜幕降临的时刻，用了同一个 night 成分。

entries.definition: The hours of darkness, another compound on night.
entries.definitionCN: 黑夜的那段时间，另一个用 night 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: A dream that frightens or disturbs the sleeper, the plain phrase for the dream sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使睡着的人恐惧或不安的梦，是「噩梦」义的普通说法。

entries.definition: Extreme fear, the feeling a nightmare leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的恐惧，是噩梦留下的感觉。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of fear and shock, often caused by something seen or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的恐惧与震惊，常由所见或想象之物引起。

entries.definition: A male demon said to lie upon sleepers, the learned name for the old nightmare creature.
entries.definitionCN: 传说中压住睡者的男性恶魔，是旧时 nightmare 所指之物的书面名称。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Old English word for night to a demon that was blamed for a weight on the chest, and its later senses keep that picture of helpless fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把古英语的「夜」与一个被归咎于胸口重压的恶魔连在一起，后来的义项都保留着那种无力恐惧的画面。

normal.en: Niht is the Old English word for night, so the first half of nightmare is simply the dark hours.
normal.cn: niht 是古英语的「夜」，所以 nightmare 的前半就是那段黑暗的时间。

normal.en: Mare in this word is a demon, not a female horse; the shared spelling is a coincidence of two unrelated words.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 mare 是恶魔，不是母马；拼写相同只是两个无关词偶然撞在一起。

normal.en: The demon was blamed for the choking weight felt during sleep paralysis, which is why the word first meant that oppression.
normal.cn: 睡眠瘫痪时感到的压身窒息被归咎于这个恶魔，所以这个词最初指的就是那股压迫。

normal.en: The dream sense came later, when the demon was forgotten and only the terror of the dream remained.
normal.cn: 「梦」这个意思来得更晚：恶魔被遗忘之后，只剩梦里的恐惧留在词里。

normal.en: The figurative sense grows straight out of the dream: a nightmare journey is a waking experience that feels equally out of control.
normal.cn: 比喻义直接从梦里长出来：a nightmare journey 就是一段同样失控的清醒经历。

abstract.en: A word invented to explain a weight on the chest ends up naming a broken schedule, because both feel like something sitting on you that you cannot push off.
abstract.cn: 一个原本用来解释胸口重压的词，最后用来命名被打乱的日程，因为两者都像有东西压在身上、推不开。

abstract.en: Nightmare keeps two unrelated words in one shell, the demon and the horse, and only the demon shaped the meaning.
abstract.cn: nightmare 把一个恶魔和一个母马两个无关的词装进同一个外壳，真正塑造词义的只有那个恶魔。

abstract.en: Every figurative nightmare is a claim that the daytime world has started behaving like a bad dream, with no exit until you wake.
abstract.cn: 每一个比喻意义上的 nightmare，都是在说白天的世界开始像噩梦一样运转，不醒来就找不到出口。

examples.en: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
examples.cn: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。

examples.en: The flooding turned the rescue into a nightmare for the whole team.
examples.cn: 洪水让整个救援队陷入噩梦般的困境。

examples.en: He still has nightmares about the accident.
examples.cn: 他仍会梦到那场事故。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈特妹儿」——夜里有个黑影压在身上，想喊也喊不出声；nightmare 就是噩梦。

root: 古英语 niht（夜）加 mare（传说中压住睡者的恶灵，一般认为与表示母马的 mare 无关）；词义由「夜间压身的恐惧」扩展为噩梦与可怕处境。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a night terror caused by a weight on the chest; the senses then divide into the bad dream, the old demon, and the waking situation that feels the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是夜里胸口受压带来的恐惧；义项由此分出噩梦、旧时的恶魔，以及感觉相同的清醒处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy dark shape at the bedside pressing on the chest while the sleeper cannot speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：床边一团沉重的黑影压住胸口，睡着的人说不出话。

branches.en: a child sitting up in the dark, calling for a parent
branches.cn: 孩子在黑暗里坐起来喊父母

branches.en: an old woodcut of a demon crouched on a sleeper's chest
branches.cn: 一幅旧木刻里蹲在睡者胸口的恶魔

branches.en: the same choking weight described first as a spirit, then as a dream
branches.cn: 同一种压身的窒息感，先说成恶灵，后说成梦

branches.en: a cancelled flight turning a holiday into a nightmare
branches.cn: 航班取消，把假期变成噩梦

branches.en: a schedule so tight that every delay spreads
branches.cn: 紧到任何延误都会扩散的日程

intro.en: The word is held together by the Old English noun for night, the demon word mare, the compound they formed and the English endings that build its adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「夜」、指恶魔的 mare、二者合成的复合词，以及构成形容词和副词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The mare in nightmare is a demon of Germanic folklore, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: nightmare 里的 mare 是日耳曼民间传说中的恶魔，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

scene: 黄昏的走廊里排着十九级台阶，最后一级上放着一支点亮的蜡烛。Her birthday falls on the nineteenth of May.

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighteenth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighteenth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第十八之后的数
senses.example: She finished nineteenth in a field of forty runners.
senses.exampleCN: 她在四十名跑者中排名第十九。
senses.why: Nineteenth is nine plus -teen plus -th: the teen ending marks ten added to a unit, and the ordinal ending marks a place in a line, so the word counts the spot just before twenty.
senses.whyCN: nineteenth 是 nine 加 -teen 再加 -th：-teen 表示十加个位数，序数词尾 -th 标出它在一列中的位置，所以这个词数的正是紧挨二十之前的那一位。

senses.title: One of nineteen equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nineteen equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成十九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A nineteenth of the profit went to the local fund.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的十九分之一拨给了本地基金。
senses.why: The same ordinal ending that ranks an item also cuts a whole into that many pieces, so a nineteenth is the share created by dividing by nineteen.
senses.whyCN: 标出名次的序数词尾，同时也把整体切成同样多的份，所以 a nineteenth 就是被十九除开之后得到的那一份。

senses.title: The nineteenth day of a month
senses.definition: the day of a month numbered nineteenth, used mostly in dates
senses.definitionCN: 一个月中编号为十九的那一天，多用于日期
senses.example: The office reopens on the nineteenth.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室在十九日重新开放。
senses.why: Dates are a list of days, so the ordinal that ranks an item in a series doubles as the name of a particular day; English drops the noun day and lets the ordinal stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 日期本身就是一串日子，因此在序列里排位的序数词也兼作某一天的名称；英语省掉 day，直接让序数词单独站立。

intro.en: Nineteenth is a native English compound of nine, the teen ending and the ordinal ending, and it belongs to the Germanic number words that English never borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nineteenth 是英语本土的复合词，由 nine、表示十几的词尾和序数词尾构成，属英语从未向拉丁语借用的日耳曼数词。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构出来的；它的确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的词。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine, and it stands at the base of nineteen, ninety and nineteenth alike.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是 nineteen、ninety 与 nineteenth 共同的底座。

items.en: The ending -tīene or -tēne meant ten more, so nigontīene counted nine beyond ten.
items.cn: 词尾 -tīene 或 -tēne 表示「又多十」，因此 nigontīene 数的是十之后再添九。

items.en: The ordinal added the -tha ending used for ranking, producing the ancestor of nineteenth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -tha，形成 nineteenth 的祖先。

items.en: Modern English spells the compound nineteenth and uses it for rank, for a nineteenth part, and for the nineteenth day of a month.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词写作 nineteenth，用来表示名次、十九分之一，以及某月的十九日。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its cardinal, tens and ordinal forms; the near-meaning group places nineteenth between its neighbours on the counting line.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一个「九」的底座，收它的基数、十位与序数形式；近义组把 nineteenth 放回计数序列，看它前后相邻的词。

entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，由 ninety 加同一个 -th 词尾构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal for nine, the smallest member of the same ordinal family.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，是同一序数词族里最小的一员。

entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 词尾而不是 -teen。

entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第十九之后的序数词，为十几这一段的结尾。

entries.definitionCN: 十三到十九共用的词尾，正是 nineteenth 所属的那一组。

normalIntro.en: The word stacks three small pieces of English counting, a unit, a ten and a rank ending, and each piece explains one of its uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把英语计数的三个小零件叠在一起：一个个位数、一个「十」和一个表名次的词尾，每个零件都解释了它的一种用法。

normal.en: Nineteen is nine plus ten, so nineteenth is the ordinal of the number that sits one step before twenty.
normal.cn: 十九就是九加十，所以 nineteenth 是紧挨二十之前那个数的序数形式。

normal.en: The -teen ending means ten added to a unit, while -ty in ninety means tens; nineteenth follows the first pattern.
normal.cn: 词尾 -teen 表示十加个位数，而 ninety 里的 -ty 表示若干个十；nineteenth 走的是前一种模式。

normal.en: The -th ending turns a count into a rank, the same ending heard in fourth and twentieth.
normal.cn: 词尾 -th 把计数变成名次，和 fourth、twentieth 里听到的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: A nineteenth can also be a part, because dividing a whole by nineteen creates nineteen equal shares.
normal.cn: a nineteenth 也可以是一份，因为把整体按十九去分，就得到十九个相等的份。

normal.en: Dates use the bare ordinal, so on the nineteenth means on the nineteenth day of the month.
normal.cn: 日期直接用序数词，所以 on the nineteenth 就是在这个月的第十九天。

abstract.en: Nineteen is the last number before the round twenty, so its ordinal always sounds like a step just short of a clean boundary.
abstract.cn: 十九是整数二十之前的最后一个数，所以它的序数听起来总像差一步就到干净边界。

abstract.en: The same word can rank a runner, cut a cake into nineteen pieces and name a day, because English lets one ordinal do the work of position, fraction and date.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以给跑者排名、把蛋糕切成十九份、还给某一天命名，因为英语让一个序数词同时承担位置、分数和日期三件事。

abstract.en: Counting words are the skeleton of a language, and nineteenth shows how a unit, a ten and a rank ending stack into one short word.
abstract.cn: 计数词是语言的骨架，而 nineteenth 展示了「一个个位数、一个十、一个名次词尾」如何叠成一个短词。

intro.en: The word is assembled from the Old English nine, the teen suffix that adds ten, the ordinal ending and the English endings it still takes.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「九」、表示「再加十」的词尾、序数词尾，以及它至今仍在使用的英语词尾组装而成。

definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighty-ninth; one of ninety equal parts
core_image: 一把长尺上刻度密密麻麻，第九十格插着一面小旗
scene: 放学后的教室里，一把长尺摊在桌上，密密麻麻的刻度里，第九十格插着一面小旗。The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighty-ninth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighty-ninth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第八十九之后的数
senses.example: The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿的第九十页仍然缺失。
senses.why: Ninetieth is ninety plus the ordinal ending -th, and ninety itself is nine plus -ty; the whole word counts nine tens and then marks the place at the end of that run.
senses.whyCN: ninetieth 是 ninety 加序数词尾 -th，而 ninety 本身是 nine 加 -ty；整个词数的就是九个十，并标出这一串末尾的位置。

senses.title: One of ninety equal parts
senses.definition: each of the ninety equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成九十等份时其中的一份
senses.example: One ninetieth of the land was set aside as a reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的九十分之一被留作保护区。
senses.why: The ordinal ending both ranks an item and divides a whole, so the same form names the share produced by splitting something ninety ways.
senses.whyCN: 序数词尾既能给事物排位，也能把整体分开，于是同一个形式也用来指把东西分成九十份后得到的那一份。

intro.en: Ninetieth belongs to the native Germanic tens, where a unit numeral plus an ending for a group of ten produced ninety, and the ordinal ending then produced ninetieth.
intro.cn: ninetieth 属日耳曼语本土的十位数：个位数词加上表示「一组十」的词尾造出 ninety，再加序数词尾便得到 ninetieth。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; the exact reconstructed shape is inferred rather than recorded.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构出来的；确切的重构形状属于推断，而不是有记录的词。

items.en: Nigon meant nine and stands at the head of the whole family, including ninety and ninetieth.
items.cn: nigon 意为「九」，是包括 ninety 与 ninetieth 在内的整个词族的源头。

items.en: The ending -tig meant a group of ten, so nigontig counted nine tens and became the ancestor of ninety.
items.cn: 词尾 -tig 表示「一组十」，因此 nigontig 数的是九个十，成为 ninety 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the tens word as nineti, and the ordinal was formed by adding the usual -th ending.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个十位数写作 nineti，序数形式则由加常见的 -th 词尾构成。

items.en: Modern English has ninetieth for a rank and, much less often, for a ninetieth part.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ninetieth 表示名次，较少用来表示九十分之一。

note.en: The look-alike group walks the same nine base up through its unit, teen, tens and ordinal forms; the near-meaning group sets ninetieth against the ordinals around it on the hundred scale.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个「九」的底座，从个位、十几、十位走到序数形式；近义组把 ninetieth 放到百的尺度上，与前后相邻的序数对照。

entries.definition: The cardinal that ninetieth ranks, nine tens in one word.
entries.definitionCN: ninetieth 所排的基数，一个词里装着九个十。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nine, the smallest member of the same -th family.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，同一 -th 词族里最小的一员。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nineteen, formed with the teen pattern rather than the tens pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 十九的序数词，用十几的模式而不是十位的模式构成。

entries.definition: The unit numeral that every member of this family starts from.
entries.definitionCN: 整个词族共同出发的个位数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal ten steps below ninetieth on the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 同一尺度上比第九十低十级的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal for one hundred, the next round landmark above ninety.
entries.definitionCN: 一百的序数词，是九十之上下一个整数地标。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position, the class of ninetieth.
entries.definitionCN: 标出位置的数词，ninetieth 所属的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word is a tens numeral wearing a rank ending, and its parts record the two steps that made it: nine tens, then a place at the end of the run.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个披着名次词尾的十位数，它内部的零件记录了造出它的两步：先有九个十，再标出这一串末尾的位置。

normal.en: Ninety is nine tens, so ninetieth marks the last place in the ninth block of ten.
normal.cn: 九十就是九个十，所以 ninetieth 标出第九个十里最后的那一位。

normal.en: The -ty ending in ninety means a group of ten, while -teen in nineteen means ten added on; ninetieth follows the first pattern.
normal.cn: ninety 里的 -ty 表示一组十，而 nineteen 里的 -teen 表示再加十；ninetieth 走的是前一种模式。

normal.en: Adding -th to ninety turns a count into a rank, exactly as fourth is built from four.
normal.cn: 在 ninety 后加 -th，就把计数变成名次，和 fourth 由 four 构成完全一样。

normal.en: The same -th form can also cut a whole into ninety equal shares, giving one ninetieth.
normal.cn: 同一个 -th 形式也能把整体切成九十等份，得到 one ninetieth。

normal.en: In dates and lists the ordinal appears alone, so the ninetieth needs no noun after it.
normal.cn: 在日期和清单里序数词单独出现，所以 the ninetieth 后面不必再跟名词。

abstract.en: Ninety is a number people reach by counting tens, so its ordinal always sounds like the close of a long even run.
abstract.cn: 九十是人们一个个数十才到达的数，所以它的序数听起来总像一长串整齐步子走到收尾。

abstract.en: A word that ranks a page can also name a share of land, because English lets one ending do both jobs.
abstract.cn: 一个能给书页排名的词，也能命名一份土地，因为英语让同一个词尾兼做两件事。

abstract.en: The tens words are the most regular part of English counting, and ninetieth shows the pattern almost without a seam.
abstract.cn: 十位词是英语计数里最规整的部分，而 ninetieth 几乎不带缝隙地展示了这个模式。

examples.en: The ninetieth page of the manuscript is still missing.

examples.en: One ninetieth of the land was set aside as a reserve.
examples.cn: 这片土地的九十分之一被留作保护区。

examples.en: They held a party for her ninetieth birthday.

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English nine, the suffix for a group of ten, the resulting tens numeral and the ordinal ending that ranks it.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「九」、表示一组十的词尾、由此得到的十位数，以及给它排名的序数词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: English nine and Latin novem descend from the same ancient Indo-European numeral, so the Latin forms are cognates listed for comparison rather than as the source.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 同出古老的原始印欧语数词，因此下列拉丁形式只是同源对照，不是来源。

definition_en: the number equal to nine times ten; also the years of a decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine, and ages in that range

scene: 清晨的旧货市场里，摊主把硬币十个一摞码成九摞，最后一摞正好压到旧布的边缘。The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.

senses.title: The number nine times ten
senses.definition: the number equal to nine groups of ten, written with the digits nine and zero
senses.definitionCN: 等于九组十的数，写作九与零
senses.example: The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。
senses.why: Ninety is a native Germanic tens word: nine plus an ending that means a group of ten, so the word itself says nine tens rather than naming a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninety 是日耳曼语本土的十位词：九加上表示「一组十」的词尾，所以这个词自己就在说「九个十」，而不是给一个新数量另起名字。

senses.title: The decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine
senses.definition: the period of ten years in a century numbered from ninety to ninety-nine, usually written the nineties
senses.definitionCN: 一个世纪里编号从九十到九十九的那十年，通常写作 the nineties
senses.example: The building was put up in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼建于九十年代。
senses.why: A century is a run of hundred years, so the last ten can be named by the tens word that opens them; English uses the plural to mean the whole span, not one year.
senses.whyCN: 一个世纪是一百年的长串，最后十年可以用开启它的那个十位数来命名；英语用复数表示整段，而不是单独一年。

senses.title: An age between ninety and ninety-nine
senses.definition: the ages from ninety to ninety-nine, especially in the phrase in one's nineties
senses.definitionCN: 从九十岁到九十九岁之间的年龄，尤用于 in one's nineties 这一说法
senses.example: She is still writing in her nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她九十多岁仍在写作。
senses.why: An age range is also a span of ten, so the same plural serves for a person's tenth decade; being in the nineties means living inside that stretch.
senses.whyCN: 年龄区间同样是一段十岁，于是同一个复数也用来指人生的第十个十年；in one's nineties 就是活在那一段里。

intro.en: Ninety is one of the native tens numerals English builds by joining a unit to an ending for a group of ten, and its plural later took on the meaning of a decade.
intro.cn: ninety 是英语本土的十位数之一，由个位数加表示「一组十」的词尾拼成；它的复数后来又承担了「十年」的意思。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants, and the exact shape of that base is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的，这个底座的确切形状存疑。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of both the tens numeral and the ordinal.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是这个十位数与对应序数词的共同底座。

items.en: The ending -tig meant a group of ten, so nigontig said nine tens in one word.
items.cn: 词尾 -tig 表示「一组十」，因此 nigontig 用一个词说出九个十。

items.en: Middle English kept the tens numeral as nineti and used the plural for groups and repeated counts.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个十位数保留为 nineti，并用复数表示多组或反复计数。

items.en: Modern English uses ninety as a number and the nineties for a decade, an age range and temperatures near ninety.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ninety 表示数目，用 the nineties 表示十年、年龄区间以及九十度上下的温度。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps to words built on the same nine base; the near-meaning group puts ninety on the same number line as its neighbours and the ten-year span it names.
note.cn: 形近组只收建在同一个「九」底座上的词；近义组把 ninety 放回同一条数轴，与相邻的数以及它所代表的那段十年对照。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nine, sharing the same base.

entries.definition: The tens number ten below ninety.

entries.definition: The round number above ninety, the next landmark on the scale.
entries.definitionCN: 九十之上的整数，是尺度上的下一个地标。

entries.definition: A group of twenty, an older English way of counting in tens and twenties.
entries.definitionCN: 一组二十，是英语较早按十与二十计数的说法。

entries.definition: A period of ten years, the unit that makes the nineties a span.
entries.definitionCN: 十年的一段时间，正是让 nineties 成为一段的单位。

normalIntro.en: The word is nine plus an old ending for a group of ten, and its plural extends the number into a decade and a decade of a life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」加上一个表示「一组十」的古老词尾，它的复数形式又把数目伸向十年和人生的十年。

normal.en: Ninety is nine tens: nine plus the -ty ending, which came from an Old English word for a group of ten.
normal.cn: 九十就是九个十：九加上 -ty 词尾，这个词尾来自古英语里表示「一组十」的词。

normal.en: The same base gives nineteen with -teen and ninety with -ty, so the two endings tell you whether ten is added or multiplied.
normal.cn: 同一个底座加上 -teen 得到 nineteen，加上 -ty 得到 ninety，两个词尾告诉你十是被加还是被乘。

normal.en: Ninetieth is ninety plus -th, the ordinary way English turns a count into a rank.
normal.cn: ninetieth 是 ninety 加 -th，正是英语把计数变成名次的寻常做法。

normal.en: The plural nineties names both a decade and an age range, because each is a block of ten years.
normal.cn: 复数 nineties 既指一个年代，也指一个年龄段，因为两者都是一块十年的长度。

normal.en: Ninety-nine is the last number before the next hundred, so ninety sits at the top of the two-digit tens.
normal.cn: 九十九是下一个百之前的最后一个数，所以九十站在两位数十位数的顶端。

abstract.en: A number made by stacking nine groups of ten carries its own explanation inside it, which is why tens words feel so transparent.
abstract.cn: 一个由九个十堆起来的数，把自己的解释藏在词里，所以十位词读起来总显得透明。

abstract.en: The jump from number to decade costs no new word, because a decade is simply ten counted one after another.
abstract.cn: 从数目跳到年代不需要另造新词，因为一整个年代不过是把十一个个数下去。

abstract.en: Ninety marks the last stretch before a hundred, the point where counting starts to feel like a rounder kind of arithmetic.
abstract.cn: 九十标出百之前的最后一段，正是计数开始变得像整块算术的地方。

intro.en: The word joins the Old English nine to the ending for a group of ten, and its plural and ordinal forms are ordinary English building on that base.

definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighth; one of nine equal parts

scene: 楼道里的九级台阶被擦得很亮，最上面一级放着一块小小的铜牌。He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.

derivatives.zh: 由 ninth 加 -ly 构成，义为「第九（用于列举）」
ninth 的基数形式，古英语 nigon 一路传下来，义为「九」

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第八之后的数
senses.example: He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。
senses.why: Ninth is nine plus the old ordinal ending -th, the same ending that makes fourth from four; the ending marks a place in a line, not a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninth 是 nine 加古老的序数词尾 -th，和 four 变 fourth 用的是同一个词尾；这个词尾标出的是一列中的位置，而不是一个新数量。

senses.title: One of nine equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nine equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A ninth of the students chose the longer course.
senses.exampleCN: 九分之一的学生选了那门较长的课程。
senses.why: The ordinal ending also cuts: a ninth is what one gets when a whole is split nine ways, which is why the rank word and the fraction word look identical.
senses.whyCN: 这个序数词尾同时也起切割作用：把整体分成九份，得到的就是 a ninth，所以表示名次的词和表示分数的词长得一模一样。

intro.en: Ninth is the ordinal of nine, formed in Old English by a unit numeral plus the ending that marks rank, then trimmed into its modern spelling.
intro.cn: ninth 是九的序数词，在古英语里由个位数词加表名次的词尾构成，后来缩减成今天的拼写。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的；确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的形式。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of the whole ordinal family.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是整个序数词族的底座。

items.en: The ordinal added the -þa ending used for ranking, giving the ancestor of ninth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -þa，形成 ninth 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English shortened and respelled the word as ninthe, and the modern consonant pattern was already visible.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短并改写为 ninthe，现代的辅音格局那时已经看得出来。

items.en: Modern English fixes the spelling ninth and uses it both for rank and for the fraction one of nine equal parts.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 ninth，并用它同时表示名次与九等份中的一份。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its teen, tens, ordinal and adverb forms; the near-meaning group places ninth between its neighbours and next to the idea of a fraction.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个「九」的底座，收十几、十位、序数与副词形式；近义组把 ninth 放到相邻序数之间，并与分数的概念放在一起。

entries.definitionCN: 九的十几形式，用 -teen 而不是序数词尾构成。

entries.definition: The tens form of nine, built with -ty.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on ninth with -ly, used in lists.
entries.definitionCN: ninth 加 -ly 构成的副词，用于列举。

entries.definition: The ordinal for ninety, part of the same -th family.
entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，属同一 -th 词族。

entries.definition: The ordinal just before ninth in the same line.
entries.definitionCN: 同一序列中紧挨在第九之前的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal just after ninth, closing the single digits.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第九之后的序数词，为个位数的结尾。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position, the class of ninth.
entries.definitionCN: 标出位置的数词，ninth 所属的类别。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, the kind of quantity one ninth expresses.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一份，正是九分之一所表达的量。

normalIntro.en: The word is nine wearing the ordinary English rank ending, and the same form serves as a rank and as a share because the ending does both jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」披上寻常的英语名次词尾；同一个形式既是名次也是一份，因为这个词尾兼做两件事。

normal.en: Nine plus -th is the same pattern as four plus -th; ninth is the ninth place, not a new quantity.
normal.cn: 九加 -th 和四加 -th 是同一个模式；ninth 是第九个位置，不是一个新数量。

normal.en: The old ordinal ending survives in modern English even though the Old English spelling has been trimmed away.
normal.cn: 古老的序数词尾在现代英语里仍然活着，尽管古英语的拼写已经被削掉。

normal.en: Ninth also divides: cut a whole into nine equal pieces and each piece is a ninth.
normal.cn: ninth 也用来分：把整体切成九个等份，每一份就是一个 ninth。

normal.en: Ninthly is built on ninth with -ly, the way English turns an ordinal into a list marker.
normal.cn: ninthly 是在 ninth 后加 -ly 造出来的，英语就这样把序数变成列举时的标记。

normal.en: Dates and floors use the bare ordinal, so on the ninth or the ninth floor needs no extra noun.
normal.cn: 日期和楼层都用光秃秃的序数词，所以 on the ninth 或 the ninth floor 不用再加名词。

abstract.en: One short ending does two jobs at once, ranking a floor and cutting a cake, which is why the same word can point in two directions.
abstract.cn: 一个短词尾同时干两件事：给楼层排名，把蛋糕切开，所以同一个词能指向两个方向。

abstract.en: Ninth is the last single-digit ordinal, so it sounds like the end of the simplest counting line.
abstract.cn: ninth 是个位数里的最后一个序数词，听起来像最简单那条计数线的收尾。

abstract.en: The word barely changed shape across a thousand years, which makes it a small fossil of how English counts.
abstract.cn: 这个词一千年里形状几乎没变，因此它是英语如何计数的一小块化石。

senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为 7 的元素，非金属，其双原子形式含牢固的三键
senses.example: Nitrogen has seven protons and typically seven neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 氮有七个质子，通常也有七个中子。
senses.why: The name labels an element, not just the air gas, so it also applies to nitrogen atoms inside proteins and fertilisers.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字标的是元素而非仅仅是空气里的气体，因此蛋白质与肥料中的氮原子同样适用。

senses.title: The bulk gas of the air
senses.titleCN: 大气主体：约占空气五分之四的惰性气体
senses.definition: molecular N2, the inert gas that dilutes oxygen and fills most of the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 双原子分子 N₂，稀释氧、占据大气绝大部分的惰性气体
senses.example: Crisp packets are filled with nitrogen to stop the contents going stale.
senses.exampleCN: 薯片包装充入氮气，防止内容物变陈。
senses.why: Because the triple bond makes N2 unreactive, industry values it precisely for doing nothing.
senses.whyCN: 由于三键使 N₂ 极不活泼，工业看重的恰恰是它「什么都不做」。

senses.title: Soil fertility and fixation
senses.titleCN: 土壤氮素：固氮、施肥与轮作
senses.definition: the nitrogen available to plants in soil, supplied by fertiliser or by bacteria that fix atmospheric gas
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中可供植物利用的氮，来自肥料或固氮细菌
senses.example: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil through their root nodules.
senses.exampleCN: 豆科植物通过根瘤给土壤补充氮。
senses.why: Plants cannot use N2 directly, so agricultural usage names the usable forms, not the gas overhead.
senses.whyCN: 植物无法直接利用 N₂，因此农业用法指的是可利用的形态，而不是头顶上的气体。

senses.title: Inside proteins
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质中的氮：氨基酸的基本成分
senses.definition: the nitrogen bound in amino acids, and therefore in every protein and in DNA
senses.definitionCN: 结合在氨基酸中、从而存在于每种蛋白质与 DNA 中的氮
senses.example: Every amino acid carries at least one nitrogen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 每种氨基酸都至少带有一个氮原子。
senses.why: Life's chemistry is built on nitrogen-containing groups, so the element doubles as a marker of protein content.
senses.whyCN: 生命的化学建立在含氮基团之上，因此这个元素也成了蛋白质含量的标记。

senses.title: Liquid nitrogen
senses.titleCN: 液氮：极低温的冷却与保存介质
senses.definition: nitrogen cooled to about minus 196 degrees Celsius, used for freezing, storage and cooling
senses.definitionCN: 冷却到约零下 196 摄氏度的氮，用于冷冻、保存与降温
senses.example: Samples are stored in liquid nitrogen at the tissue bank.
senses.exampleCN: 组织库中的样本保存在液氮里。
senses.why: The boiling point of the gas is so low that its liquid becomes a standard laboratory coolant.
senses.whyCN: 这种气体的沸点极低，其液态因此成了实验室的标准冷却剂。

senses.title: Nitrogen oxides and smog
senses.titleCN: 氮氧化物：交通排放与光化学烟雾
senses.definition: the family of nitrogen-oxygen compounds, especially NO and NO2, formed in hot engines and driving photochemical smog
senses.definitionCN: 氮与氧的化合物一族，尤其是高温引擎生成的 NO 与 NO₂，会促成光化学烟雾
senses.example: Nitrogen oxides from traffic feed the smog over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 交通排放的氮氧化物助长了谷地上空的光化学烟雾。
senses.why: Pollution control needed a short collective label, so the element name stands in for its troublesome compounds.
senses.whyCN: 污染控制需要一个简短的统称，于是元素名被用来指代它那些麻烦的化合物。

senses.title: The nitrogen cycle
senses.titleCN: 氮循环：在空气、土壤与生物之间流转
senses.definition: the circulation of nitrogen among the atmosphere, soil, water and living things through fixation, assimilation and denitrification
senses.definitionCN: 氮经固氮、同化与反硝化在大气、土壤、水体与生物之间循环
senses.example: The nitrogen cycle moves the element between air, soil and living things.
senses.exampleCN: 氮循环让这个元素在空气、土壤与生物之间流转。
senses.why: Because the element changes chemical form at every step, the cycle is named after the element rather than any one compound.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个元素在每一步都改变化学形态，循环便以元素而非某一种化合物命名。

senses.title: The nitre-former in the name
senses.definition: the sense recorded by the name itself: Chaptal named the gas because it was found in nitre, that is, saltpetre
senses.definitionCN: 名字本身记录的义项：夏普塔尔因这种气体存在于硝石（硝酸钾）中而为它命名
senses.example: The name nitrogen still says 'nitre-former', though the gas itself is inert.
senses.exampleCN: nitrogen 这个名字至今仍表示「硝石产生者」，尽管这种气体本身是惰性的。
senses.why: The French coinage nitrogene described where the element came from chemically, and English simply transliterated the claim.
senses.whyCN: 法语造词 nitrogene 描述的是该元素在化学上的来源，英语只是把这个说法音译过来。

intro.en: Nitrogen is a French scientific coinage of 1790, built from Greek nitron 'soda, nitre' and -genes 'producer'. Its first element was already ambiguous in ancient Greek.
intro.cn: nitrogen 是 1790 年的法语科学造词，由希腊 nitron「碱、硝石」与 -genes「产生者」构成。它的第一块在古代希腊语中就已含混。

items.en: Greek nitron named native soda, a mineral salt used in cleaning, not saltpetre. Latin nitrum later shifted the word toward saltpetre, and chemistry inherited the confusion.
items.cn: 希腊 nitron 指天然碱，一种用于洗涤的矿物盐，而非硝石。拉丁 nitrum 后来把这个词引向硝石，化学继承了这一混淆。

items.en: The suffix -genes 'born of, producing' comes from the root gen- 'to be born'. It marks the element as something that generates a named substance.
items.cn: 后缀 -genes「由……所生、产生」出自词根 gen-「出生」。它把这个元素标记为能生成某种特定物质的东西。

items.en: In 1790 the French chemist Chaptal coined nitrogene, because the gas was obtained from nitre and seemed to be the nitre-forming principle. The claim was later revised.
items.cn: 1790 年法国化学家夏普塔尔造出 nitrogene，因为这种气体可从硝石取得，似乎是成硝石的本原。这一说法后来被修正。

items.en: English nitrogen appears in the 1790s, transliterating the French term as the new chemistry spread. Before that the gas was called 'dephlogisticated air' or 'mephitic air'.
items.cn: 英语 nitrogen 在 1790 年代出现，随新化学的传播音译了法语术语。在此以前，这种气体被称作「脱燃素空气」或「毒气」。

items.en: Once the element rather than the compound became the unit of chemistry, nitrogen named element 7 and its compounds were renamed as nitrides, nitrates and oxides.
items.cn: 当化学的单位从化合物转为元素后，nitrogen 成为 7 号元素的名称，其化合物则改称氮化物、硝酸盐与氧化物。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and whether Chaptal or a colleague first suggested the form nitrogene is debated; Greek nitron itself has no agreed deeper origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见的确切书证年代存疑，nitrogene 这一形式由夏普塔尔还是其同僚最先提出仍有争议；希腊 nitron 本身的更深来源也无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words sharing the nitre root whose chemistry differs sharply; the second holds other atmospheric gases that are often confused with nitrogen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「硝石」词根但化学性质差别很大的词；第二组是常与氮混淆的其他大气气体。

entries.definition: A salt or ester of nitric acid, containing the NO3 group, such as potassium nitrate in fertiliser. Nitrogen is the element; nitrate is one of its compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 硝酸的盐或酯，含 NO₃ 基团，如肥料中的硝酸钾。nitrogen 是元素，nitrate 是它的化合物之一。

entries.definition: A salt containing the NO2 group, used in cured meat and formed in soil as an intermediate step of nitrification.
entries.definitionCN: 含 NO₂ 基团的盐，用于腌肉，也在土壤中作为硝化过程的中间产物生成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'containing nitrogen', as in nitrogenous waste. It describes a material, not the element itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「含氮的」的形容词，如含氮废物。它描述材料，而不是元素本身。

entries.definition: The gas that makes up about a fifth of the air and supports combustion and respiration. Nitrogen dilutes it and does not burn.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气五分之一、支持燃烧与呼吸的气体。氮稀释它，且自身不燃烧。

entries.definition: A noble gas making up about one percent of the air, even less reactive than nitrogen. It is used where an absolutely inert atmosphere is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气百分之一的稀有气体，比氮更不活泼。需要绝对惰性气氛时就用它。

entries.definition: NH3, a pungent gas made industrially from nitrogen and hydrogen. It is the form in which nitrogen is turned into fertiliser.
entries.definitionCN: NH₃，工业上用氮与氢合成的刺激性气体。它正是氮被转化为肥料时所采取的形态。

definition_zh: 没有人；谁都不；小人物；无名之辈
definition_en: not a single person, and also a person of no importance or influence
core_image: 一间本该坐满人的屋子，椅子全是空的
scene: 会议室的门开着，桌上的杯子还冒着热气，可一圈椅子全是空的。Nobody came to the meeting, so the chairs stayed empty all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 nobody 是「没有一个人」（第 1 个义项：在场的人一个也没有）；句意为没有人来开会，椅子整个下午都空着。图中可辨识物件：冒热气的杯子、空椅子、开着的门。

derivatives.zh: 由 no 与 one 组合而成，与 nobody 同义，语气更正式
由前缀 non- 加 entity 构成，义为「无足轻重的人」

senses.title: Not a single person
senses.definition: not one person; no person at all, used when the number of people present is zero
senses.definitionCN: 一个人也没有；表示在场人数为零
senses.example: Nobody was waiting at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站里没有一个人在等。
senses.why: The word welds the negator no onto body, so it denies not an action but the very existence of a human figure in the scene.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把否定词 no 焊在 body 上，否定的不是某个动作，而是场景里是否存在一个具体的人。

senses.title: A person of no importance
senses.definition: an ordinary or unimportant person, especially one without fame or influence
senses.definitionCN: 普通而不重要的人，尤指没有名声或影响力的人
senses.example: He was a nobody before the film made him famous.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部电影让他出名之前，他只是个无名小卒。
senses.why: Once nobody rules out any important figure, the phrase can be turned into a countable noun that names the missing importance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当 nobody 排除了任何重要人物之后，这个说法就能变成可数名词，直接指那份缺失的分量。

senses.title: No person except
senses.definition: used in the pattern nobody but to mean no person other than the one named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 nobody but 结构，表示除了提到的这个人之外没有别人
senses.example: Nobody but the guard saw him leave.
senses.exampleCN: 除了门卫，没有人看见他离开。
senses.why: The negator still empties the scene of people, and but then names the single exception hidden inside that emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 否定词仍然把场景里的人清空，but 随后点出藏在这片空无之中的唯一例外。

intro.en: Nobody is an English compound of the negator no and the noun body, first recorded in the fourteenth century and not borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nobody 是英语否定词 no 与名词 body 的复合，最早见于十四世纪，并非借自拉丁语。

items.en: The Old English negator nā meant not or no, and it is the ancestor of modern no.
items.cn: 古英语否定词 nā 意为「不、没有」，是现代 no 的前身。

items.en: Bodig meant the body, the physical frame of a person, and became modern body.
items.cn: bodig 指身体、人的躯体，后来演变为 body。

items.en: In the fourteenth century the two words were joined as nobody, a pronoun meaning no person.
items.cn: 十四世纪这两个词合成 nobody，作代词表示「没有人」。

items.en: Writers began using a nobody as a countable noun for a person of no account.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作家开始用 a nobody 这个可数名词，指无足轻重的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps both uses and adds the plural nobodies for several unimportant people.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两种用法，并加上复数 nobodies 来指多个无足轻重的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pronouns built from the same body element; the near-meaning group gathers words for absence of people and for insignificance.
note.cn: 形近组收以同一个 body 成分构成的一组代词；近义组收表示「没有人」以及「无足轻重」的词。

entries.definition: A person whose name and background are not recognised.

normal.en: Split the word in two: no plus body, meaning no body is there.
normal.cn: 把它拆成两半：no 加 body，意思是现场没有一个身子。

normal.en: The spelling is one word, but the stress stays on the first part, NO-body.
normal.cn: 拼写上它是一个词，重音却落在前半部分：NO-body。

normal.en: Nobody takes a singular verb: nobody knows, never nobody know.
normal.cn: nobody 接单数动词：说 nobody knows，不说 nobody know。

normal.en: The same body ending builds anybody, somebody and everybody.
normal.cn: 同一个 body 词尾还构成 anybody、somebody 与 everybody。

normal.en: When it names unimportant people, it becomes countable: one nobody, two nobodies.
normal.cn: 当它指无足轻重的人时，就变成可数：一个 nobody，两个 nobodies。

abstract.en: A word that denies every human figure turns the whole scene into an empty room.
abstract.cn: 一个否定所有人影的词，把整个场景变成一间空屋。

abstract.en: The same word can then name the emptiness itself, which is how a person becomes a nobody.
abstract.cn: 同一个词随后可以指那份空无，于是一个人就被说成了小人物。

abstract.en: Nobody is language doing a head count and finding zero.
abstract.cn: nobody 是语言点了一遍人头，然后报出零。

definition_zh: 点头；点头示意；打盹；致意
definition_en: to move the head quickly down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement, and also to fall asleep briefly
core_image: 下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位
scene: 散会后，他没有开口，只朝门口等着的同事低了下头，随即转身离开。He gave her a brief nod and walked out of the room.
sceneCN: 这里 nod 是「点头示意」（第 1 个义项：以点头表示问候或同意）；句意为他朝她轻轻点了下头，就走出了房间。图中可辨识物件：半开的会议室门、走廊里的同事、手里的文件。

derivatives.zh: nod 加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「点头的；（花枝等）低垂的」
nod 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er，义为「点头的人」

senses.title: To move the head down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement
senses.definition: to move the head quickly down and up, especially to greet someone or to show that you agree
senses.definitionCN: 快速地把头低下再抬起，尤用于问候别人或表示同意
senses.example: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest visible yes: the head dips and returns, and the whole body quietly accepts what has just been said.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一个看得见的「是」：头低下去又回来，整个身体就安静地接受了刚才听到的话。

senses.title: To fall asleep briefly, especially when you should stay awake
senses.definition: to begin to sleep accidentally for a short time, often while sitting or listening
senses.definitionCN: 在不该睡的时候不小心睡着一小会儿，常发生在坐着或听讲时
senses.example: He nodded off during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。
senses.why: The same drooping motion that signals sleepiness ends in a real loss of attention, so the verb stretches from a greeting to a head that falls forward and stays down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个耷拉下去的动作本是困意的信号，最后却变成真正的走神，于是词义从问候扩到「头垂下去、撑不住睡着」。

senses.title: A single quick movement of the head
senses.definition: a single quick movement of the head down and back up, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 头快速低下再抬起的一次动作，用作某种信号
senses.example: She answered with a quick nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点了一下头作为回答。
senses.why: When the gesture is seen as an event rather than an act, the same word becomes a noun that counts each dip of the head.
senses.whyCN: 当这个手势被看成一件发生的事，而不是一个动作时，同一个词就变成名词，数得清每一次低头。

senses.title: An act of acknowledgement or tribute
senses.definition: a gesture, design or remark that openly acknowledges or honours someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示认可或致敬的动作、设计或言辞
senses.example: The new building is a nod to the town's fishing past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新建筑是在向小镇的渔业历史致意。
senses.why: A small gesture of recognition is enough to say that something deserves respect, so the word widens from the head movement to any quiet sign of approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个很小的致意动作，就足以说明某样东西值得尊重；于是词义从头部的动作扩展到任何安静的认可。

intro.en: Nod is first recorded in Middle English, and its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally treated as an expressive gesture word rather than a borrowing from Latin.
intro.cn: nod 最早记录于中古英语，更早的来源不确定；一般认为它是模仿动作的表达性词语，而不是借自拉丁语。

items.en: The verb appears first in Middle English, and no reliable older root has been established; most dictionaries mark its origin as uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词最早出现在中古英语，没有可靠的更早词根被确认；多数词典都标注其来源不确定。

items.en: Nodden meant to make a quick bowing movement of the head, close to the modern gesture.
items.cn: nodden 意为把头快速低一下，和现代的手势已经很接近。

items.en: The word is attested in writing from the fourteenth century with the sense of the head movement.
items.cn: 这个词从十四世纪起见于书面记录，表示头部的这一动作。

items.en: The phrase nod off appears for falling asleep in a chair, adding the sleep sense to the family.
items.cn: nod off 这个说法出现，用于在椅子上睡着，为这个词族添上了「打盹」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, uses the noun for the gesture, and extends a nod to to mean tribute.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词，用名词指这个动作，并把 a nod to 扩展为致敬之意。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on nod, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other small signals and other words for light sleep.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nod 构成的形式，另收一个只是长得像的词；近义组收其他细小的示意动作，以及表示浅睡的词。

entries.definition: A short sleep, usually planned, during the day.

normalIntro.en: The word is probably an expressive gesture word, and its family keeps circling small head movements, approval and sudden sleep.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很可能是模仿动作的表达性词语；词族始终围绕头部的细微动作、许可以及突然的睡意。

normal.en: A nod is one dip and return, unlike a bow, which bends the whole upper body.
normal.cn: 点头只是一次低头再抬起，与弯下整个上身的鞠躬不同。

normal.en: The past form doubled the final consonant: nod becomes nodded, not noded.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写词尾辅音：nod 变成 nodded，不是 noded。

normal.en: Nod off stretches the gesture into sleep, as if the head dips and never comes back.
normal.cn: nod off 把这个动作拖成了睡眠，好像头低下去就再没抬回来。

normal.en: Get the nod means to be approved or chosen, because approval was once given with a silent nod.
normal.cn: get the nod 表示获准或被选中，因为过去常以一个无声的点头表示同意。

normal.en: A nod to is figurative: the head gesture becomes a sign of respect for something old.
normal.cn: a nod to 是比喻用法：点头这个动作变成了对旧事物的尊重。

abstract.en: A gesture too small for words carries a complete yes, which is why nodding survives in every crowded room.
abstract.cn: 一个小到不需要言语的动作，却承载了完整的「是」，所以点头在每个拥挤的房间里都还活着。

abstract.en: The same downward motion marks both politeness and exhaustion, and the language keeps both in one word.
abstract.cn: 同一个向下的动作，既表示礼貌，也表示疲惫，而语言把它俩留在同一个词里。

abstract.en: Nod is the body answering before the mouth has decided what to say.
abstract.cn: nod 是身体在嘴巴想好说什么之前，先替它作了回答。

examples.en: The director gave the young actor the nod.
examples.cn: 导演点头选中了那位年轻演员。

definition_zh: 吵闹地；大声地；喧嚷地；发出嘈杂声地
definition_en: in a way that makes a lot of loud sound, or with loud and insistent complaint
core_image: 声音挤出门缝，沿着走廊一路推过来
scene: 午休时间，走廊尽头那间教室的桌椅被推来推去，碰撞声一直传到办公室。The boys were arguing noisily behind the closed door.
sceneCN: 这里 noisily 是「吵闹地、大声地」（第 1 个义项：以很大的声音做事）；句意为男孩们在关着的门后大声争吵。图中可辨识物件：被推动的课桌、走廊尽头关着的门、办公室的窗户。

derivatives.zh: 由 noise 加 -y 构成，义为「吵闹的；嘈杂的」

senses.title: In a loud and disturbing way
senses.definition: with a lot of loud sound that disturbs the people around
senses.definitionCN: 发出很大的声响，打扰到周围的人
senses.example: The children played noisily in the yard until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在院子里吵闹地玩到天黑。
senses.why: The adverb takes the adjective noisy and adds -ly, so the sound leaves the object and becomes the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由形容词 noisy 加 -ly 构成，于是声音从物体身上离开，变成做一件事的方式。

senses.title: With loud complaint or protest
senses.definition: with loud and insistent complaint, so that everyone nearby can hear it
senses.definitionCN: 以响亮而执拗的抱怨表达不满，让附近的人都听得见
senses.example: The crowd protested noisily outside the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在市政厅外大声抗议。
senses.why: When a group wants to be heard, volume becomes a tool of pressure, and the same manner word shifts from mere sound to public demand.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体希望被听见时，音量就成了施压的工具；同一个方式副词于是从单纯的声音转向公开的诉求。

senses.title: With much clatter from things or machines
senses.definition: with a continuous clatter or rattle, usually made by machines or objects rather than by people
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着持续的碰撞声或咔嗒声，通常来自机器或物件而不是人
senses.example: The old printer ran noisily all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧打印机整夜响个不停。
senses.why: Objects make noise without intending anything, so the adverb can simply name the clatter that comes along with their working.
senses.whyCN: 物件本身并无意图，却照样发出声响，所以这个副词也能单纯描述它们运转时伴随的嘈杂。

intro.en: Noisily is the adjective noisy plus the adverb ending -ly; the deeper origin of noise is uncertain, and one common suggestion links it to Latin nausea through Old French.
intro.cn: noisily 是形容词 noisy 加副词词尾 -ly；noise 更早的来源不确定，一种常见的说法认为它经古法语与拉丁语 nausea 有关。

items.en: The ultimate source of noise is uncertain; dictionaries often record a suggested link with Latin nausea, but that link is not proved.
items.cn: noise 的最终来源不确定；词典常记下一种与拉丁语 nausea 相关的猜测，但这条线索并未得到证实。

items.en: Old French noise meant quarrel, outcry or din, and it could name a loud dispute as well as a loud sound.
items.cn: 古法语 noise 意为争吵、喊叫、喧闹，既可指大声的争执，也可指响亮的声响。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word for a loud outcry or a confusing din before it settled as the general term for unwanted sound.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个词，先指大声喊叫或杂乱的喧闹，后来才固定为「不受欢迎的声音」的通用说法。

items.en: The adjective noisy was formed with -y, and the adverb noisily followed with -ly.
items.cn: 形容词 noisy 由 -y 构成，副词 noisily 随后由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Modern English uses noisily for the manner of an action, especially play, speech and machines.
items.cn: 现代英语用 noisily 描述动作的方式，尤其见于玩耍、说话和机器运转。

entries.definitionCN: 以粗野、混乱而吵闹的方式。

entries.definition: With a loud and continuous demand or outcry.

normalIntro.en: The word is built from noise through two endings, and its family keeps turning sound into a quality and then into a manner of acting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 noise 经两个词尾层层构成；词族不断把声音变成性质，再变成做事的方式。

normal.en: Noise plus -y gives noisy, and noisy plus -ly gives noisily.
normal.cn: noise 加 -y 得 noisy，noisy 再加 -ly 得 noisily。

normal.en: The y at the end of noisy turns into i before -ly: noisily, not noisyly.
normal.cn: noisy 末尾的 y 在 -ly 前变为 i：写作 noisily，不是 noisyly。

normal.en: Noisy sits before a noun, while noisily sits beside a verb and tells how it is done.
normal.cn: noisy 放在名词前，noisily 则靠近动词，说明动作是怎么做的。

normal.en: The comparative uses more and most, never noisilier.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more 与 most，不说 noisilier。

normal.en: The noun behind the whole family is noise, an uncountable word for unwanted sound.
normal.cn: 整个词族背后的名词是 noise，用来指不受欢迎的声音，通常不可数。

abstract.en: A sound becomes a habit of a place, then a quality of a thing, then a way of acting.
abstract.cn: 一种声音先变成一个地方的习惯，再变成事物的性质，最后变成做事的方式。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers children at play and a crowd demanding to be heard, because volume is both joy and pressure.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词既描述玩耍的孩子，也描述要求被听见的人群，因为音量既是快乐，也是压力。

abstract.en: Noisily is what a room sounds like when nobody inside remembers that others are near.
abstract.cn: noisily 是一间屋子里的人忘了隔壁还有别人时，那间屋子听起来的样子。

scene: 楼上那户人家的地板从晚饭后就没安静过，脚步和音乐声一直传下来。The upstairs neighbours were noisy again, and the whole floor stayed awake.

senses.title: Making or full of loud, disturbing sound
senses.definition: making a lot of loud sound, or filled with sound that disturbs people
senses.definitionCN: 发出很大的声响，或充满扰人的声音
senses.example: The street outside the hotel was noisy all night.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆外面的街道整夜都很吵。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns the noun noise into a quality, so a place or person can be described as carrying that sound wherever it goes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把名词 noise 变成一种性质，于是一个地方或一个人就被描述成走到哪里都带着这种声音。

senses.title: Lively with many people and sounds
senses.definition: full of people, music and activity in a way that feels lively rather than merely annoying
senses.definitionCN: 人多、有音乐、有活动，气氛活跃，而不只是令人烦躁
senses.example: It was a noisy party, with music and laughter in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个热闹的聚会，每个房间都有音乐和笑声。
senses.why: Loud sound is not always a complaint; when many people gather happily, the same quality becomes a sign of life and energy.
senses.whyCN: 响亮的声音并不总是抱怨的对象；当许多人聚在一起高兴时，同一种性质就成了生气与活力的标志。

senses.title: Containing unwanted random variation
senses.titleCN: 有噪声的；夹杂随机误差的
senses.definition: containing random error or interference that hides the true signal, used of data, images or measurements
senses.definitionCN: 含随机误差或干扰，掩盖了真实信号，用于数据、图像或测量
senses.example: The sensor produced noisy data whenever the motor started.
senses.exampleCN: 马达一启动，传感器就会产生有噪声的数据。
senses.why: In technical use the unwanted sound of everyday life becomes unwanted variation in a signal, and the same word follows the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 在技术语境里，日常生活里不受欢迎的声音变成信号中不受欢迎的波动，同一个词顺着这个比喻继续使用。

items.en: The ultimate source of noise is uncertain; a connection with Latin nausea is often suggested but cannot be confirmed.

items.cn: 中古英语借入时指大声喊叫，后来缩小为不受欢迎的声音。

items.en: Noise received the ending -y to form noisy, the adjective of a place or person full of sound.
items.cn: noise 加上词尾 -y 构成 noisy，用来形容充满声音的地方或人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense and adds the technical sense of data disturbed by random error.
items.cn: 现代英语保留日常义，并增加了「数据受随机误差干扰」的技术义。

entries.definition: So loud that it seems to block out every other sound.

normal.en: Noise plus -y gives noisy: full of noise.
normal.cn: noise 加 -y 得 noisy：充满噪声的。

normal.en: A noisy party is not an insult: the same word can signal fun instead of disturbance.

abstract.en: The word shows how easily a nuisance turns into a sign of life, depending on who is listening.

abstract.en: Noisy is the sound of a building with all its windows lit.
